chunks: So bear with patience, as the apostles who were constant, bore; and do not be hasty (in demanding punishment) for them. On the day they see what they had been foretold, (they will realise) that they did not stay in the world but only an hour of the day. This is the message to be conveyed: Shall any perish but the ungodly?
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the patience of the prophets and the brevity of worldly life?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'Ulul-Azm' refers specifically to the five arch-prophets (Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad), establishing a model of resilient endurance for the Imams and the faithful during times of tribulation. The verse reassures believers that the perceived delay in divine justice is merely a brief moment in the eternal perspective of God, encouraging steadfastness rather than impatience. It concludes by identifying the 'Fasiqun' (transgressors) as the sole recipients of destruction, highlighting the moral dimension of patience.
